location_name: Taiping Island (Itu Aba), Tizard Bank, Spratly (Nansha) Islands
summary: In September 1980 eight civilian researchers of the Taiwan Provincial Fisheries Research Institute went to Taiping Island to conduct research, and on 25 September they officially registered their domiciles (household registration) on the island, the first civilian residents recorded there; the Institute's ship surveyed the waters around Tizard Bank as a fishing ground.
actors: Taiwan Provincial Fisheries Research Institute; ROC household-registration authorities (Kaohsiung)
reasoning: Registering civilian residents on a held feature and sending a state research ship to survey its waters are unilateral administration without confrontation; demonstrative, and new in kind (first civilian domiciles on Taiping, which the MOFA cites as evidence of habitation). The MOFA source is a PDF, so the excerpt cannot be machine-checked; the second source (Smith 1994, Internet Archive text) dates the survey to September 1980 and judges the area uneconomical for Taiwan's fishing.

summary: The first Townhall Meeting (citizens' assembly) for residents of the Nansha Region was held on Taiping Island on 16 November 1980, following the registration of civilian domiciles there in September.
actors: ROC local administration for the Nansha Region; civilian residents of Taiping Island (Fisheries Research Institute staff)
reasoning: Holding a local civic assembly for registered residents of a disputed feature is a unilateral act of civil administration; demonstrative, low salience, and a coder may fold it into the 25 September domicile event. The source is a PDF, so the excerpt cannot be machine-checked; no second source was found.

summary: The state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corporation (CPC) sent a team to Taiping Island and drilled a geological exploration well to a depth of 523 metres; it encountered only coral-reef strata and did not establish the presence of oil or gas.
reasoning: Exploratory drilling by a state company on a disputed feature is unilateral resource activity; demonstrative, and new in kind for Taiwan (no earlier ROC hydrocarbon drilling in the Spratlys is recorded). The source, a 2019 ministerial report to the Legislative Yuan reported by CNA, gives only ROC year 70 (1981); Chinese Wikipedia dates the team to June 1981 citing a 2013 CNA story that is no longer online, so the month is unverified.

actors: ROC government (fishermen service station on Taiping Island; garrison)
reasoning: Providing state services to fishermen from a held feature is unilateral administration supporting the claimant's fishing presence; demonstrative, low salience. The Coast Guard's 'Historical Background' gives only the year; the source is the English translation filed as Annex 910 in a PCA PDF, so the excerpt cannot be machine-checked. Wikipedia (citing a National Tsing Hua University page, unreachable) dates a 'Pratas Fishermen's Service Station' to 1987 as well; the two may be confused or parallel.

summary: The ROC Minister of National Defense publicly refuted Malaysia's claims in the Spratly Islands, after Malaysia's Deputy Foreign Minister had declared that the islands and atolls within Malaysia's continental shelf were under Malaysian sovereignty.
actors: ROC Ministry of National Defense (Minister of National Defense)
reasoning: A minister's public rejection of a rival claim is a verbal assertion; declarative, and the first ROC statement aimed at Malaysia found for the decade. Known only from a one-line entry in Smith's 1994 chronology (no date within the month, no text); the Malaysian statement it answered was reported by the New Straits Times on 25 February 1988 (Dzurek 1996), so the refutation probably fell in the last days of February.

summary: In the days after the 14 March 1988 China-Vietnam clash at Johnson South Reef, the ROC Navy carried out an emergency resupply mission to its garrison on Itu Aba (Smith dates it to 17 March; Hurwitt to mid-March).
reasoning: An out-of-schedule naval resupply of a garrisoned feature during a crisis is a show of presence without confrontation; demonstrative, and more than the routine quarterly runs because it was an emergency mission. The day is uncertain (Smith's 17 March entry bundles several events), so month precision. Vietnam and China were the parties to the clash; no ROC action toward either is recorded. Reports that Taiwan let PRC ships shelter or resupply at Taiping were not found in any source opened.

summary: After the Johnson South Reef clash, Taiwan reasserted its sovereignty over the Spratlys, and the defence leadership told the Legislative Yuan that Taiwan would fight to the last man to defend Taiping Island against any aggressor.
actors: ROC Ministry of National Defense (Smith names 'Defense Minister Hao'; the minister in March 1988 was Cheng Wei-yuan and Hau Pei-tsun was Chief of the General Staff); Legislative Yuan
reasoning: A public reassertion of sovereignty and a pledge to defend the feature by force are verbal assertions; declarative (a coder may weigh the 'fight to the last man' line as an implicit threat). The speaker is misidentified or ambiguous in the only source naming him, and no date within March is given. Sun (1996) adds that the ROC defence minister indicated Taipei would, if necessary, help Beijing defend its position on the islands (citing The Economist, 21 May 1988); that remark is aimed at Vietnam and cooperative toward the PRC, and its date is unknown.

summary: In April 1988, as China and Vietnam occupied further Spratly reefs after the March clash, Taipei reinforced its garrison on Itu Aba.
actors: ROC Ministry of National Defense; Itu Aba (Taiping) garrison
reasoning: Adding troops to a held feature is a unilateral military build-up without confrontation; demonstrative, and the first reinforcement recorded since 1974. Known from one thesis (Hurwitt 1993, citing Chang Pao-min, Contemporary Southeast Asia 12(1), June 1990, pp. 28-29); size and units are not given.

summary: On 12 December 1988, the 42nd anniversary of the 1946 recovery, the ROC sovereignty monument on Taiping Island (front inscription 'Nansha Islands Taiping Island', erected 12 December 1946) was rebuilt, its side carrying the inscription 'Rebuilt 12 December, 77th year of the Republic of China'.
actors: ROC government / Taiping Island garrison (agency not named)
reasoning: Rebuilding a sovereignty marker on a held feature is a unilateral symbolic act of possession; demonstrative, low salience. The date comes from the stele's own inscription as transcribed by the Coast Guard; the source is a PDF, so the excerpt cannot be machine-checked.

summary: A national (sovereignty) monument was set up on Dongsha (Pratas) Island on 30 June 1989 to assert ROC sovereignty over the whole Pratas archipelago; Wikipedia, citing National Tsing Hua University, attributes to the Minister of the Interior a 1989 'South China Sea Defense' (南海屏障) national stele on the island.
actors: ROC Ministry of the Interior (per NTHU via Wikipedia); Pratas garrison
reasoning: Erecting a national sovereignty monument on a held feature is a unilateral symbolic act of possession; demonstrative. It is new for the Pratas in the decade and precedes the January 1990 'Lock and Key to the Southern Territory' stele on Taiping. The MOI attribution and the identity with the 南海屏障 stele rest on an unreachable NTHU page; the Coast Guard's Dongsha PDF reproduces the 南海屏障 text without a date. The PRC is the only other claimant to the Pratas, hence RC.
